test_cases.title: Navigate to Event Types from Setup menu
test_cases.description: Verify that the Event Types list page is accessible from the Setup/Configuration navigation menu
test_cases.preconditions: User is logged in with admin credentials
steps: Log in to https://staging.247software.com/ with Pranay / Pranay@1234
Locate the Setup or Configuration menu in the navigation
Click on Event Types menu item
test_cases.expected_result: Event Types list page loads without errors and displays existing event types

test_cases.title: Event Types list displays correct columns and data
test_cases.description: Verify that the Event Types list shows the correct column headers and data rows
test_cases.preconditions: User is on the Event Types list page
steps: Navigate to Event Types list page
Observe the table/list headers and content
test_cases.expected_result: List shows at minimum a Name column; existing records are displayed without UI errors

test_cases.title: Create a new Event Type with valid data
test_cases.description: Verify a new Event Type can be created successfully with a unique name
test_cases.preconditions: User is on the Event Types list page
steps: Click the Add / New / Create button on the Event Types list page
Enter a unique Event Type name: 'TestEventType_Auto'
Fill in any other required fields with valid values
Click Save / Submit
test_cases.expected_result: New event type 'TestEventType_Auto' is created and appears in the list; a success notification is shown

test_cases.title: Create Event Type form contains required fields and controls
test_cases.description: Verify the Create Event Type form has all required input fields and action buttons
test_cases.preconditions: User is on the Event Types list page
steps: Click the Add / New button
Observe the form that appears
test_cases.expected_result: Form is displayed with at minimum a Name field and Save/Cancel buttons

test_cases.title: Edit an existing Event Type successfully
test_cases.description: Verify that an existing Event Type can be edited and changes are persisted
test_cases.preconditions: At least one Event Type exists in the system
steps: Navigate to Event Types list
Click the Edit/pencil icon on an existing Event Type
Modify the name to 'UpdatedEventType_Auto'
Click Save
test_cases.expected_result: Event Type is updated with new name 'UpdatedEventType_Auto'; the list reflects the change; a success message is shown

test_cases.title: Edit form pre-populates existing values
test_cases.description: Verify the edit form loads with the current saved values pre-filled
test_cases.preconditions: At least one Event Type exists
steps: Navigate to Event Types list
Click Edit on an existing record
Observe the form fields
test_cases.expected_result: All form fields are pre-populated with the current saved values of the selected Event Type

test_cases.title: Delete an Event Type successfully
test_cases.description: Verify that an Event Type can be deleted and is permanently removed from the list
test_cases.preconditions: At least one deletable Event Type exists (e.g., 'TestEventType_Auto')
steps: Navigate to Event Types list
Click the Delete/trash icon on the target Event Type
Confirm the deletion in the confirmation dialog
test_cases.expected_result: Event Type is removed from the list; a success notification is shown; record no longer appears on page refresh

test_cases.title: Cancel delete keeps Event Type in list
test_cases.description: Verify cancelling the delete confirmation dialog does not remove the Event Type
test_cases.preconditions: At least one Event Type exists
steps: Navigate to Event Types list
Click Delete on an Event Type
Click Cancel in the confirmation dialog
test_cases.expected_result: Event Type remains in the list unchanged; no deletion occurs

test_cases.title: Validation error shown when Event Type name is empty
test_cases.description: Verify required-field validation fires when the name is left blank on submit
test_cases.preconditions: Create Event Type form is open
steps: Click Add to open the Create form
Leave the Name field blank
Click Save / Submit
test_cases.expected_result: A validation error message is displayed indicating the Name field is required; no record is created

test_cases.title: Validation error shown for whitespace-only Event Type name
test_cases.description: Verify that a name consisting only of spaces is rejected as invalid
test_cases.preconditions: Create Event Type form is open
steps: Click Add to open the Create form
Enter only spaces in the Name field
Click Save
test_cases.expected_result: A validation error is shown; whitespace-only input is not accepted as a valid name

test_cases.title: Duplicate Event Type name is rejected with error
test_cases.description: Verify that creating an Event Type with an already-existing name produces a duplicate-entry error
test_cases.preconditions: An Event Type named 'TestEventType_Auto' already exists in the system
steps: Click Add to open the Create form
Enter 'TestEventType_Auto' (existing name) in the Name field
Click Save
test_cases.expected_result: An error message is displayed indicating the name is already in use; no duplicate record is created

test_cases.title: Newly created Event Type appears in downstream selector
test_cases.description: Verify that a newly created Event Type is available in event-type dropdowns elsewhere in the application
steps: Navigate to a section that uses an Event Type dropdown (e.g., Incident creation form)
Open the Event Type selector/dropdown
Search or scroll for 'TestEventType_Auto'
test_cases.expected_result: The newly created Event Type is available as an option in the downstream selector

test_cases.title: Search input narrows Event Types list correctly
test_cases.description: Verify the search or filter input on the Event Types list returns matching results
test_cases.preconditions: Multiple Event Types exist in the list
steps: Navigate to Event Types list
Type a partial name into the search/filter input
Observe the list results
test_cases.expected_result: Only Event Types matching the search term are displayed in the list

test_cases.title: Search with no matching term shows empty state
test_cases.description: Verify that searching for a non-existent Event Type shows an appropriate empty/no-results message
test_cases.preconditions: Event Types list page is open
steps: Enter a search term that matches no existing Event Type (e.g., 'XYZNONEXISTENT999')
Observe the list
test_cases.expected_result: List shows empty state or 'No results found' message with no records displayed

test_cases.title: Admin user has full CRUD access to Event Types
test_cases.description: Verify admin-role user can view, create, edit and delete Event Types
steps: Navigate to Event Types
Verify Add, Edit, and Delete controls are visible
Confirm each control is functional
test_cases.expected_result: Admin user sees and can use all CRUD controls on Event Types without permission errors

test_cases.title: Event Types page UI elements are correctly rendered
test_cases.description: Verify the Event Types page has correct labels, button text, and a responsive layout
test_cases.preconditions: User is on the Event Types list page
steps: Navigate to Event Types list
Inspect page title, column headers, and action button labels
Resize browser to tablet width (768px) and check responsive layout
test_cases.expected_result: Page title, labels, and buttons are correctly named; layout adapts responsively without content overflow

test_cases.title: Create Event Type with maximum allowed character name
test_cases.description: Verify system behavior when Event Type name is at the maximum character boundary
test_cases.preconditions: Create Event Type form is open
steps: Click Add to open the Create form
Enter a name of exactly 255 characters
Click Save
test_cases.expected_result: Event Type is created successfully OR a clear character-limit validation message is shown; no system error occurs

test_cases.title: Event Types page loads within acceptable performance threshold
test_cases.description: Verify that the Event Types list page fully loads within 5 seconds
test_cases.preconditions: User is authenticated and has network access to staging
steps: Navigate to Event Types list page
Measure time from navigation click to full page render
test_cases.expected_result: Page fully renders within 5 seconds on a standard broadband connection
